item.title: 関西電力、美浜原発3号機を手動停止へ
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 関西電力は17日、美浜原発3号機（福井県美浜町）の原子炉を手動停止すると発表した。機器点検の際に、放射性物質を含まない2次系の設備から水滴が落ちているのを確認したため。環境への放射能の影響はないとしている。

ただちに支障が出る事象ではないが、今後の運転に万全を期す目的などで、停止して点検することを決めた。

5月8日に高圧タービンからの蒸気漏れを確認したため原子炉を手動停止し、6月16日から定期検査を開始。9月12日に原子炉を起動したばかりだった。

item.title: 米住宅着工件数は減少、市場予想も下回る－集合住宅の急減が響く
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 8月の米住宅着工件数は減少した。集合住宅の急減が響いた格好で、新型コロナ禍以降でも最も低い方の一つとなった。

着工件数は集合住宅が21.7%減少して、35万7000戸となった。一方、一戸建て住宅は7.6%増の91万8000戸と、3月以来の高水準。西部と中西部での増加が全体をけん引した。

一戸建ての着工件数は8月に増加したものの、住宅ローン金利が上昇し、物件取得能力が圧迫される中で、住宅市場は引き続き厳しい状況にある。

在庫がコロナ禍前の水準を引き続き大幅に上回っていることから、住宅建設業者も着工の拡大に慎重になっている可能性がある。

完成した物件数は12%近く減少し、2018年12月以来の低水準。一戸建て住宅の完成件数はコロナ禍前以来の低い水準となった。

キャピタル・エコノミクスの北米担当エコノミスト、ブラッドリー・サンダース氏は「高水準かつ上昇を続ける借り入れコストが開発業者の活動を抑制している全体的な状況に変わりはない。住宅着工が今後さらなる減少傾向をたどるという当社の見方を裏付けている」と、リポートに記した。

一戸建て住宅の建設許可件数は1.8%減の87万8000戸となった。

着工件数は地域別では、全米最大の住宅建設地域である南部で1.3%減少し、3カ月ぶりの低水準。西部は5カ月ぶりの高水準となった。中西部は一戸建て住宅こそ大きく増加したが、全体としては減少した。

原題：US Housing Starts Drop Unexpectedly on Multifamily Projects (3)（抜粋）

item.title: 米新規失業保険申請は19.6万件、7月以来の低水準－祝日を含む週
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 先週の米新規失業保険申請件数は、7月以来の低水準に減少した。継続受給者数は2年超ぶりの低水準となり、労働市場の安定を示す新たな材料となった。

新規申請件数は1969年以降でも特に低い水準の1つとなった。この期間にはレーバーデーの祝日が含まれており、データは祝日前後に大きく変動することがある。

より変動の少ない新規申請件数の4週移動平均は20万3250件に減少し、5週間ぶりの低水準となった。

新規申請件数の減少には、レーバーデーや新学年の開始に伴う季節的な変動が影響した可能性がある。それでも、一部で注目を集めた人員削減を除けば、全体的な傾向からは経済全般でレイオフが低水準にとどまっていることがうかがえる。

ブルームバーグ・エコノミクス（BE）のイライザ・ウィンガー氏はリポートで、「失業保険申請件数は引き続き、レイオフ圧力が小さいことを示している。ただ、米連邦準備制度理事会（FRB）がさらに金融引き締めを進めれば、安定している労働市場が弱含むリスクがある」と指摘した。

人員削減は限定的だが、採用にばらつきがある中、米国では転職をためらう人が多く、採用も解雇も少ない労働市場の状況が一段と鮮明になっている。

季節調整前ベースでは、新規申請件数は大幅に減少した。特にカリフォルニア州やテキサス州、ミシガン州、ニューヨーク州での減少が目立った。

原題：US Jobless Claims Fall to 196,000 During Holiday Week (2)（抜粋）

item.title: Rising oil, rates and yields brew up stagflation cocktail for markets
item.description: The surge in energy and global borrowing costs as a result of the war in the Middle East is pushing economies and markets further towards a potentially damaging period of high inflation and slow growth.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Rebaudo, Harry Robertson, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: The surge in energy and global borrowing costs as a result of the war in the Middle East is pushing economies and markets further towards a potentially damaging period of high inflation and slow growth. For now, stocks remain near record highs and economic growth, thanks to the avalanche of spending on the AI boom, has been resilient. The rise in the value of oil and gas, and the increase in global government bond yields to financial crisis-era highs, has been orderly. But a growing number of metrics are showing that fragility may be creeping in. "Up until now, it's just been a commodities and rates story. It's not been an equity and credit story. We're starting to worry that we might be getting to a point where it starts having equity and credit effects," Chris Jeffery, head of macro strategy at LGIM, said of the rise in borrowing costs, rates and energy. PUMP IT UP Oil futures are back above $100 a barrel, 50% above where they were prior to the war, as intensifying attacks across the Middle East threaten more supply routes. The derivatives market shows traders aren't expecting any near-term drop in the price. Investors are betting most heavily on Brent crude at $100 by the end of December, closely followed by options to sell it at $60, highlighting the extreme uncertainty right now. It isn't just crude. Diesel is nearing record highs, jet fuel is double what it was in February before the Iran war broke out, while European natural gas is at its highest since 2022, as regional utilities vie with competitors in Asia for cargoes. Online prediction market Polymarket shows users are attaching just an 18% chance of the Strait of Hormuz reopening by December. INFLATION EXPECTATIONS After subsiding over the summer, inflation is picking up again. In the US, [USN:L1N452123 TEXT:"headline inflation"] held at 3.4% in August, with a 3.9% jump in gasoline prices. Europe tells the same story. Euro zone [USN:L1N44T095 TEXT:"annual inflation"] accelerated to 3.3% in August from 2.9% in July, well above the ECB's 2% target, driven largely by energy. The UK is no better, with [USN:L8N45806W TEXT:"inflation accelerating"] to a five-month high of 3.1% in August. The European Central Bank earlier this month upped its [USN:S8N42J00V TEXT:"inflation expectations"] to an average of 2.5% next year, while underlying inflation is seen at 2.6% in 2027, from 2.5% previously. The swaps market shows inflation in the euro zone is expected to be around 3.5% next year and still only at 2.4% in five years' time . US one-year inflation expectations are close to 2.5%, with little change for the next five years. . ENERGY INCREASINGLY DRIVING RATE BETS The war has totally changed the outlook for global interest rates. Previously, markets and economists expected the world’s largest central banks to either leave rates on hold, or cut them. Traders now expect almost a full point in rate rises from the European Central Bank in the next year, and at least two more hikes for the Federal Reserve after Wednesday’s 25-bp increase. They see energy as the most influential factor in the rate outlook. The Bank of England on Thursday left rates unchanged, but said it expects UK inflation to top 4% — double its target — by early 2027, from a previously forecast peak of 3.2% by late 2026. The [USN:L1N459138 TEXT:"Bank of Japan"] raised rates to a 31-year high on Friday and signalled its readiness to keep pushing up borrowing costs. GROWTH HEADWINDS BUILD So far this year, countries’ economies have powered through the headwinds. PMI scores - closely watched measures of the private sector - pointed to [USN:S0N4490C8 TEXT:"solid expansion"] in the US and Europe in July and August. Data this week showed [USN:L8N45309X TEXT:"UK growth"] beat expectations in July, as did [USN:L1N4580DO TEXT:"US retail sales"] in August. This resilience has underpinned stock markets. Second-quarter earnings for S&P 500 companies [USN:L4N44V0YE TEXT:"are expected"] to have grown 53% year-on-year, according to LSEG I/B/E/S data. Yet energy prices look set to stay high and the [USN:L6N4570XY TEXT:"global bond selloff"] has pushed up yields on government debt, which set the tone for borrowing rates everywhere. The average US 30-year mortgage is at its highest since June 2025 above 6.7%. The question for investors is whether growth can survive higher energy and borrowing costs, just as doubt about the sustainability of the billions of dollars [USN:L6N45608P TEXT:"pouring into AI"] is starting to creep into investors' minds. CASH-STRAPPED Consumers are increasingly in the line of fire. The cost of fuel at the pump has soared, household energy bills are likely to do the same this winter, especially in Europe, where storage levels are at their lowest in 15 years for this time of year. Mortgage and borrowing rates are up and wage growth is not keeping pace. Investors are anticipating a slowdown. US consumer discretionary stocks (.SPLRCD) are the worst performers on Wall Street so far this year, with a drop of nearly 6%, compared with the S&P's 10% gain (.SPX) . In Europe, the contrast is even starker. Consumer discretionary stocks are down 17% this year (.SXCDP) , the second-worst performers after luxury, versus a 7.5% gain in the STOXX 600 (.STOXX) . With interest rates going up, squeezed consumers will be more likely to save, than spend, further depriving their domestic economies of oxygen.

item.title: Democratic senator calls for US diplomats to help guide Europe troop review
item.description: A key Senate Democrat has asked Secretary of State Marco Rubio to ensure that U.S. diplomats are involved in a Pentagon-led review of America's military presence in Europe that has alarmed NATO allies.
item.dc:creator: Gram Slattery
item.content:encoded: A key Senate Democrat has asked Secretary of State Marco Rubio to ensure that U.S. diplomats are involved in a Pentagon-led review of America's military presence in Europe that has alarmed NATO allies. In a letter addressed to Rubio, who is also the national security advisor, Senator Jeanne Shaheen, the top Democrat on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, wrote that diplomats, including U.S. ambassadors in potentially affected countries, are being kept out of the loop. The letter was first shared with Reuters. The review, which began in June and is [USN:L1N44O00G TEXT:"due to"] conclude by the end of the year, is part of a push by the Trump administration to have Europe rely less on the United States and instead take more responsibility for its own defense. Among the possibilities being considered by Pentagon officials, Reuters [USN:L6N459017 TEXT:"reported"] on Thursday, is withdrawing some 25,000 troops from Europe, a move that would worry European officials who are facing an increasingly confrontational Russia. The U.S. currently has around 80,000 troops stationed in Europe. "The Department of State, which is responsible for managing our bilateral relationships, has traditionally played a substantial role in reviews of this kind," read the letter. "Yet what we are hearing through our own conversations, travel across Europe and engagement with our Allies tells a different story. U.S. Ambassadors and Chiefs of Mission in affected countries have been excluded from consultations." A State Department official disputed the letter, saying that diplomats were in fact being consulted. "State Department officials, including Ambassadors, are in regular contact with DOW colleagues as the force posture review proceeds," the official said, referring to the Trump administration's name for the Pentagon. The Europe force posture review is being led by the Department of Defense, with Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby taking a leading role. The Trump administration has frequently excluded State Department personnel from policy debates relevant to their portfolios, sources have told Reuters. Those sources have generally declined to be named due to the sensitivity of the issue. Advocates of that approach say that, by keeping decision-making circles small, the administration can move quickly while minimizing leaks. Opponents say it means weighty decisions are made without sufficient input from experts and allies. Shaheen wrote that adjustments in troop levels would have an effect on bilateral relationships that the State Department would be left to manage, with the Baltic nations of Estonia, Lithuania and Latvia among the countries with the most at stake. "Even changes that may appear modest from a purely military standpoint can have outsized effects on our bilateral relationships, particularly with Baltic Allies, as Russia continues to intensify its hybrid actions along NATO's eastern flank," read the letter. European leaders have warned of [USN:L6N4580QI TEXT:"hybrid incidents"], often attributed to Russia, that fall below the threshold of conventional military attacks but undermine European security — such as sabotage, arson and drone incursions.

item.title: 英中銀、政策金利3.75%に据え置き－長期国債の売却計画を撤回
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： イングランド銀行（英中央銀行）は17日、政策金利を3.75%に据え置くと発表した。市場も据え置きを予想していた。英中銀はその一方で、中東紛争の影響でインフレ圧力が高まった場合には利上げが必要となる可能性を指摘した。

英中銀の金融政策委員会（MPC）は、6対3で据え置きを決定した。7月の前回会合と同じ結果だった。

ベイリー総裁は準備原稿で、世界的なエネルギーショックが英国の物価や賃金に及ぼしている影響はこれまでのところ限定的だとしたうえで、「しかし、この不安定な状況が長引くほどインフレへの影響は大きくなり、政策金利を引き上げる必要性も高まる」と述べた。

英中銀はまた、長期国債の売却計画を撤回し、金融緩和目的で買い入れた4880億ポンド（約101兆8000億円）規模の国債ポートフォリオのうち3680億ポンド相当のみを2034年9月までに解消すると明らかにした。

この計画は英国債市場に安心感を与え、30年債利回りはここ4カ月で最大となる10ベーシスポイント（bp、1bp＝0.01%）余り低下した。金融政策により敏感に反応する2年債利回りも低下した。

計画に基づくと、短期国債については市場で直接売却するのではなく、債務管理庁（DMO）に移管する方針で、移管の条件を詰めている間は、量的引き締め（QT）に伴う国債売却を2027年4月まで全面的に停止する。

これらの措置により、今後数カ月は国債の供給が減り、英国債市場を下支えすると見込まれている。インフレや財政への懸念から債券は世界的に売られている。

ベイリー総裁はテレビインタビューで、長期国債の売却停止を含む国債保有の圧縮計画を発表したことについては、市場に「安心感」を与えるものだと説明する一方、足元の市場の混乱への対応で政府を支援する意図があるとの見方を否定した。

ベイリー氏は「この計画には長い間取り組んできた。初夏の政権交代を受けて作業を始めたわけではないと断言できる」と強調。財務省やDMOと作業を進めており、「前政権とも取り組んでいたし、現政権とも取り組んでいる」と述べ、「特定の政権を優遇するということは一切ない」と語った。

item.title: 高市首相、金融政策の具体的手法は日銀に委ねる－利上げ観測強まる中
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： 高市早苗首相は17日の記者会見で、日本銀行の金融政策について公式見解を繰り返した。18日までの金融政策決定会合での利上げ観測が強まる中、日銀をけん制する発言はなかった。

内閣改造を受けた記者会見で語った。金融政策の具体的な手法については日本銀行に委ねられており、「そうあるべきだと考えている」と強調。日銀には政府と密接に連携し、経済・物価・金融情勢を踏まえながら、2%の物価安定目標の持続的、安定的な実現に向け、「適切な金融政策運営を行うことを期待している」とも述べた。

今回の決定会合では、政策金利を31年ぶりの高水準となる1.25%に引き上げる見通し。利上げが行われれば6月以来、3カ月ぶり。植田和男総裁の体制下では、これまで平均して半年に1回程度だった間隔から大幅な短縮となる。高市政権は従来から利上げに慎重な姿勢とみられていた。

高市首相は改造内閣について「決断と挑戦、そして実行の内閣」だと強調。「強い経済の実現に向けた政策を加速させ、日本列島を強く豊かにしていく」と語った。「成長なくして財政の持続可能性は維持できない」とも述べ、「今こそ、責任ある積極財政の実行を急がなければならない」とした。

臨時国会に関連法案を提出する飲食料品の消費税率引き下げの財源については、「市場の信認を得られるように、特例公債に頼らず確保する」とし、「ご心配をいただかなくてもよいと考えている」と説明した。「見通しはしっかり立っている」とも語ったが、具体的な財源は明言しなかった。

長期金利の指標となる新発10年物国債の利回りは9月に入り、一時3%台に到達した。昨年10月の高市政権発足以降、財政拡大への懸念が根強く、上昇傾向にある。高市首相は政権の経済財政運営に関しては丁寧に説明し、市場の信認を確保していく考えも示した。

item.title: Is NATO ready to fight? The Ukraine war is raising doubts among military analysts
item.description: The Ukraine war is raising doubts among military analysts.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Flynn, Max Hunder, Olena Harmash
item.content:encoded: Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine has killed hundreds of thousands of people. It has also served as a proving ground for new weapons systems and raised an uncomfortable question for the North Atlantic Treaty Organization: Is the alliance prepared for the next war it might have to fight? Five Ukrainian and Western defense officials told Reuters that developments on the battlefield are moving so quickly that some NATO weapons and tactics risk becoming outdated. While Ukraine – which is not an alliance member – adapts in weeks, NATO buys and develops systems over years, sometimes decades. The Ukraine war and U.S. President Donald Trump’s haranguing of European allies have prompted many NATO members to dramatically increase their defense spending. The Pentagon is currently reviewing its military presence in European countries, which Trump has accused of sponging off U.S. protection and refusing to help prosecute his unpopular war against Iran. Denys Shtilerman, the co-owner and chief designer of Fire Point, a leading Ukrainian missile and drone builder, told Reuters that tanks are now “worthless” because a drone costing about $5,000 can destroy one. Yet Europe still spends heavily on tanks – which, say many military analysts, still have a key role to play in future battles. Cheap drones have also transformed warfare in other ways. Troops gathering in groups or large vehicle convoys all become far easier targets. “They are good at storming positions,” Oleksandr Pivnenko, Commander of the National Guard of Ukraine, said of the international troops his units trained with last year. “But if there’s a drone overhead and you don’t even look up, what do you think will happen to your squad?” In June, Reuters attended a NATO military exercise near Paldiski in Estonia – a small Baltic country now fortifying its 210-mile border with Russia – in which American and European troops treated dozens of simulated casualties at wartime field hospitals. But the exercise took place with the assumption that NATO would command the airspace above the hospitals – no longer a given in the age of cheap, stealthy, long-distance drones. Rather than simply receiving NATO training and assistance, Ukrainian officials described a growing role for Ukraine in teaching the alliance lessons drawn from the war with Russia. Yet they also said NATO’s military bureaucracy struggles to absorb those lessons. A Ukrainian officer who underwent NATO psychological operations training in Romania told Reuters that some alliance training materials still relied on case studies from World War Two. NATO didn’t respond to questions about the officials’ criticism of its training and bureaucracy. The Ukraine war has also exposed a vulnerability that NATO officials say is far harder to solve: air and missile defense. Russia’s relentless barrages against Ukrainian cities have highlighted Europe's dependence on sophisticated U.S. anti-missile systems such as the Patriot, first used in the 1991 Gulf War. Ukraine has a critical shortage of Patriot interceptors – the missiles fired to destroy incoming threats. Fearing that its reliance on Patriots might become a strategic vulnerability, Europe is building non-U.S. alternatives. Ukraine is awaiting delivery of the new French-Italian SAMP/T-NG air-defense system, designed to intercept ballistic missiles. France has [USN:L8N44J026 TEXT:"promised to accelerate its deployment"] to Ukraine, and European diplomats previously told Reuters it was expected to arrive by next spring. In a statement, the Ukrainian defense ministry said its soldiers and NATO’s had much to learn from each other, hailing Ukraine’s use of drones and radioelectronic warfare as “globally unmatched" and praising European efforts to help tackle Russia’s drone and missile bombardments. In July, Ukraine and nine European allies launched an [USN:L8N43E02V TEXT:"air-defense coalition"] that includes plans to jointly develop a new anti-ballistic missile system. Known as Freyja, the project is a consortium of about a dozen companies with Fire Point as the lead private-sector partner. The goal is to build a system that is cheaper and faster to produce than the Patriot, while ensuring that Europe, not the U.S., controls its manufacture. “If you spend $20 billion on your air defense system, you must be independent in your security,” said Fire Point’s Shtilerman.

item.title: In Silicon Valley, AI data center boom meets local resistance
item.description: A clash with residents and environmental groups highlights a challenge confronting policymakers nationwide.
item.dc:creator: Elizabeth Mendez, Nichola Groom
item.content:encoded: In Silicon Valley's biggest city, residents and environmental groups are organizing against a wave of proposed data center projects that officials have courted in a bid to position the city as a hub for AI infrastructure. The clash highlights a challenge confronting policymakers nationwide: how to support an industry viewed by government and business leaders as critical to economic competitiveness while responding to growing public concerns about the electricity, water and pollution impacts of the infrastructure required to power it. In California, that debate is particularly fraught because the state is home to many of the companies driving the AI boom, including Google (GOOGL.O) , Meta (META.O) , OpenAI and Anthropic. San Jose, a city of nearly 1 million and California's third-largest, has embraced the industry's growth. Last year, city leaders announced an agreement with utility PG&E (PCG.N) to speed delivery of power to large energy users such as data centers. The city estimates each new facility could generate between $3 million and $6 million in tax income annually for services such as police, fire protection, libraries, roads and parks. Despite Silicon Valley's wealth, however, many residents remain unconvinced that the benefits of the wave of tech-driven growth tied to AI-focused facilities will be broadly shared. "The companies have to prove to us why they deserve our resources and how they're going to give back to the community," said Ellina Yin, a leader of the grassroots I Love San Jose coalition. Yin and others are pushing for stricter public review, more transparency around energy and water use and studies of health and environmental impacts before more projects are approved. Mayor Matt Mahan says the answer is not to halt data center development but to ensure it is done responsibly. "People are right to question, 'Is this pushing up my energy costs? Is it using our clean water supplies? Will it degrade quality of life in my city?'" Mahan told Reuters. "These are very fair questions." The fight comes as California Governor Gavin Newsom weighs a package of bills intended to protect state residents from the costs of powering data centers and increase transparency around their energy and water use. PG&E said new large customers can help spread fixed grid costs across a broader customer base and help lower bills. Air quality is a particular concern. In April, a coalition led by the Center for Biological Diversity petitioned the Bay Area Air Quality Management District to strengthen oversight of diesel backup generators used at data centers, arguing that existing regulations predate the recent expansion of AI-related facilities. The district said it is exploring whether stronger protections are warranted. NEW LEGISLATION PENDING The concerns raised in San Jose have increasingly made their way to Sacramento, California's capital. Lawmakers recently gave final approval in both the state Senate and Assembly to several bills addressing data centers, including measures intended to ensure large electricity users pay their share of grid-related costs and requirements aimed at increasing transparency around energy and water consumption. State Senator Steve Padilla, who authored several of the measures, said California has an obligation to lead because it is home to many of the world's largest technology companies. The Data Center Coalition, an industry trade group whose members include Google, Meta, OpenAI and Anthropic, said it supports responsible growth but argued the bills unfairly single out data centers rather than other large industrial and commercial electricity users. The group warned the measures could discourage investment and push jobs, tax revenue and projects to other states. Newsom has until the end of the month to either sign or veto the legislation. His office declined to comment because the bills are pending before the governor.

item.title: インド首相、半導体企業誘致に本腰－米2社から大規模投資引き出す
item.description: （ブルームバーグ）：
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded:
（ブルームバーグ）： インドのモディ首相は17日に始まった国内最大の半導体業界イベントで、世界の半導体製造で主要国の一角に食い込むというインドの大胆な取り組みを印象付け、米国のアプライド・マテリアルズとラムリサーチから数十億ドル規模の投資計画を引き出した。

モディ氏はニューデリーで3日間の日程で開かれる「SEMICON」でスピーチし、エンジニアリングを学んだ働き手の多さや半導体産業を後押しする政策を、外国企業が活用すべき強みだとしてアピール。「世界は今、新たな信頼できる製造拠点を切実に必要としている」と述べ、「インドは絶えず態勢を整えている」と強調した。

モディ氏は10年前にはほとんど存在しなかったインドの半導体・電子機器産業の利点を強く訴え、世界の半導体メーカーのほか、インドの国産企業にとって潜在的な提携先や顧客となる企業、さらにはAI投資の波に乗ろうとする製造装置メーカーや部品供給会社の誘致を図っている。

世界最大の人口を抱え、長年にわたり世界の多くの国を上回る経済成長を遂げてきたインドにとって、その成否は極めて重要だ。

モディ政権は経済のさらなる近代化を進めるとともに、輸出を強化して成長を持続させる取り組みの一環として、半導体など付加価値の高い産業の拠点となる力がインドにあることを示そうとしている。製造業の拡大は、農業からより賃金の高い仕事へ多くの労働者を移すという政権構想にとって不可欠だ。

ベンガルール（旧バンガロール）のシンクタンク、タクシャシラ・インスティテューションのプラナイ・コタスタネ副所長は、「半導体産業の成長にインドが長期的に取り組む姿勢を示すモディ氏の手段がニューデリーでのSEMICONだ」と指摘し、「それが世界の投資家に向けた首相のメッセージだ」と述べた。

今回のイベントには、世界の300社が集結。出展者数は600を超え、150人余りが講演する。スタートアップの展示や学生向けのイベントもある。

item.title: Equinor signs long-term LNG agreement with Thailand's PTT Trading
item.description: Equinor said on Friday it has signed a long-term agreement to supply liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Thailand's PTT Trading (PTTT).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Equinor (EQNR.OL) said on Friday it has signed a long-term agreement to supply liquefied natural gas (LNG) to Thailand's PTT Trading (PTTT). "The agreement underlines the role of LNG in contributing to security of supply in a dynamic energy market," Equinor's senior vice president for gas and power, Helle Oestergaard Kristiansen, said in a statement. Equinor said it already supplies crude oil and refined products to PTTT on a regular basis and aims to further develop the relationship through the LNG agreement. The Norwegian company produces LNG at a plant in Arctic northern Norway and also buys LNG from US producer Cheniere for deliveries to its own customers, a business it is [USN:L4N4580A9 TEXT:"looking to expand"]. Equinor said the commercial terms were confidential, and declined to comment on the duration and volume of the contract.
